Derivability is membership in the admitted instances or coverage by a uniform all-tuples rule, and no other inference exists. The profile of a datum is the set of well-formed contexts whose plugging is derivable. Two data are collapsed when their profiles are equal and separable when some well-formed context is derivable for one and not the other; that is the declared sense used for every separation requirement.

summary: Let B_2(Q) be the invertible upper-triangular 2x2 matrices over Q, T the diagonal matrices and N the unit upper-triangular matrices. Every invertible element factors uniquely as D * n with D in T and n in N, and conjugation of an element of N by an invertible element stays in N. torusProj preserves multiplication. On any vertex type with a root, a parent function and a depth function that strictly decreases along parents, and for invertible labels off the root, root-to-vertex transport multiplies labels on the left: T(root) = I and T(v) = U(v) * T(parent(v)). The stage-one field u_N(v) equals D(v) * n(v)^{-1} * D(v)^{-1}, lies in N, and equals [[1, -b(v)/d2(v)], [0, 1]]. Dressing a tree edge by u_N yields D(child) * D(parent)^{-1}. For every label g and every pair of vertices, torusProj(u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) equals torusProj(g). A further diagonal vertex field, multiplied on the left at the child and on the right by its inverse at the parent, leaves that dressed tree edge diagonal. The stage-two field u_T(v) = D(v)^{-1} satisfies u_T(v) * u_N(v) = T(v)^{-1}, and u_T(target) * (u_N(target) * g * u_N(source)^{-1}) * u_T(source)^{-1} equals T(target)^{-1} * g * T(source). That dressed label equals I if and only if g = T(target) * T(source)^{-1}. A vertex field that is invertible at every vertex, equals I at the root, and satisfies U(v) = g(v) * g(parent(v))^{-1} off the root, equals the rooted transport. The factorization identity fails on [[0, 1], [0, 1]]. Replacing the (2, 2) entry by 1 does not preserve the product of [[2, 1], [0, 3]] with itself. On any commutative ring, the operators (bA)(u, v, w) = -A(u, w) and (A smile A)(u, v, w) = A(u, v) * A(v, w) satisfy b composed with b equal to 0, the Bianchi identity for K = bA + A smile A, and endpoint gauge covariance K(A^g) = g(u) * K(A) * g(w)^{-1} when A^g(x, y) = g(x) * A(x, y) * g(y)^{-1}. For A(0,1)=1, A(1,2)=1, A(0,2)=0, g(0)=1 and g(1)=2, the source-only expression (g(0)*A(0,1))*(g(1)*A(1,2)) - (g(0)*A(0,2)) is not equal to g(0)*(A(0,1)*A(1,2) - A(0,2)). The same values with g(2)=1 and g(1)^{-1}=1/2 satisfy the endpoint identity. The arithmetic comparison of 2 with 3 records that these integers differ. On the four-vertex tree with parents 0, 0, 0, 2, transport at vertex 3 equals U(3) * U(2).

A doubled positive carrier has distinct normalized states with identical product statistics.

summary: The conic hull of represented available effects equals PSD for arbitrary finite n<=m with m nonzero, using the verified state cone, sound effects, all local binary product tests and calibrated local-unitary and controlled-shift pullbacks. name: Binary effects and explicit effect saturation
obligation: EffectSaturated is a separate no-restriction premise, not a consequence of state-cone or generated-effect-cone equality. Local complex QM and the state-reconstruction assumptions remain supplied.

Homogeneous bounds are equivalent to probabilities in [0,1] on all trace-one PSD states. Soundness plus explicit EffectSaturated identifies the available binary effects with this full interval.

Conversely every such POVM is available under both EffectSaturated and the separate FiniteTestSaturated premise. The end-to-end quantum_measurements theorem invokes quantum_state_cone and returns the generated cone, binary interval and finite-POVM equivalence.

obligation: The six-forest count, the order-0 collapse, and the quotient 7 are recorded only for these three edge sets and this numerator. summary: On the declared overlapping edge sets L = {0,1,2}, R = {2,3,4} and G = {0,1,2,3,4}, a Zimmermann forest is a subset whose members are pairwise nested or disjoint, and the forests are exactly the six subsets in which L and R do not both occur. For the declared numerator N(x,y) = 2 + 3x + 5y + 7xy that sum is 7xy, so the quotient by xy equals 7 wherever xy is nonzero. The three-forest sum that omits G equals 7xy - 2, and its quotient is 7 - 2/(xy). At (x,y) = (1/2, 1/3) the two quotients are 7 and -5. Algebraic cancellation for actual Feynman-parametric integrands, and any use of this identity before continuum integration, is not established.

name: Does the obstruction a quantum computation generates limit its own ability to finish reliably
obligation: The finite model answers the question as a threshold condition (QCV-Q1 to QCV-Q6); whether any physical system meets the named assumptions is not derived and no verdict on physical viability is given.
summary: Every step of a noisy quantum computation, syndrome extraction and repair included, adds residual, and repair consumes capacity while adding residual of its own; the question is whether this makes reliable completion a self-referential no-go or a threshold condition that holds only under named resource assumptions (fresh supply, net-efficient repair, bounded overhead growth, physical error below threshold).

obligation: lam, g, kappa and r are declared inputs; no value is derived or measured for any code, and Phi_1 of a residual is not computed here.
summary: Backlog q(t+1) = max(0, q(t) + lam + g*mu - mu) in units of the Phi_1 repair cost, where lam is the residual generated per round by the computation, mu = kappa*r the repair rate from r fresh ancillas per round at kappa units each, and g the residual generated per unit of repair; with g = 0 this is the DS-QM101 queue; a distance-three level with a fault locations has constant c = a(a-1)/2.

name: Backlog is bounded exactly when the net repair rate covers generation; unit-gain repair never bounds it
obligation: A statement inside the declared model; it does not say any code has g < 1 or that any supply r is available.
summary: In the QCV-Q1 model with q0 >= 0, the backlog is bounded iff lam <= (1-g)*mu; for g >= 1 and lam > 0 no mu >= 0 bounds it; for g < 1 and mu = kappa*r, with kappa > 0, it is bounded iff r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa); with r = 0 and lam > 0 it equals q0 + t*lam.

obligation: The location counts are declared; nothing here says how many repair locations a physical code needs.
summary: The union-bound recurrence p(k+1) = a*p(k) with a >= 1 and p(0) > 0 does not tend to zero; for 2 <= a <= b fault locations the certified threshold 1/pairCount(b) is at most 1/pairCount(a).

obligation: Exact constants and noise hypotheses of each theorem are not reproduced; the finite recurrence in QCV-Q2 is the only part checked.
summary: The fault-tolerance threshold theorems (Shor 1996; Aharonov and Ben-Or 1997; Kitaev 1997; Knill, Laflamme and Zurek 1998; Aliferis, Gottesman and Preskill 2006) are cited under each theorem's own noise, locality and overhead hypotheses; they are not re-proved.

name: Concatenation recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2: exact closed form and threshold dichotomy over the rationals
obligation: The recurrence is the hypothesis; no noise model is shown to obey it and no constant c is computed for any code.
summary: For the recurrence p(k+1) = c*p(k)^2 over Q, c*p(k) = (c*p(0))^(2^k); for c > 0 and p(0) >= 0: if c*p(0) < 1 then p(k) tends to zero with c*p(k) <= (c*p(0))^(k+1) and, for c*p(0) <= 1/2, p(k) <= (1/2)^(2^k)/c; if c*p(0) = 1 then p(k) = 1/c for all k; if c*p(0) > 1 then p(k) diverges; so p(k) tends to zero iff p(0) < 1/c.

name: Exact criterion on a level-dependent overhead for the existence of a threshold region
obligation: The families are exact illustrations of the criterion, not claims that any physical overhead has such a form; correlated-noise strength as an exponential of block size is a declared toy.
summary: For p(k+1) = c(k)*p(k)^2 with c(k) >= 0, p(k) = p(0)^(2^k)*amp(k) with amp(0) = 1, amp(k+1) = c(k)*amp(k)^2, and some p(0) > 0 has p(k) tending to zero iff some M > 0 has amp(k) <= M^(2^k) for all k; the criterion holds for c(k) <= C, for c(k) <= A*B^(k+1) with A, B >= 1, for c(k) = (k+1)^2, and for c(k) <= a*b^N(k) with block size N(k+1) <= s*N(k), s < 2; it fails for c(k) >= a*b^(2^k) with a > 0, b > 1, and for c(k) >= a*b^N(k) with 2^k <= N(k), b > 1, where no positive p(0) has p(k) tending to zero.

name: Limitations of noisy reversible computation without fresh bits (literature)
obligation: The exact statement and its noise model are in the cited paper; QCV-Q4 establishes a finite exact analogue for global depolarizing noise only.
summary: Aharonov, Ben-Or, Impagliazzo and Nisan (1996) show that noisy reversible or quantum computation with no supply of fresh low-entropy bits cannot preserve its input beyond a short depth; the result is cited, not re-proved or imported as a proof here.

name: Trace distance of two noisy unitary histories without fresh resources decays by the product of one minus the noise rates
obligation: The trace norm is the variational form, whose equality with the sum of singular values is cited; the noise is global depolarizing with a declared rate per step, not independent per-qubit noise, and the statement is about histories without fresh resets.
summary: For complex matrices of any size d and the variational trace norm tn(X) = sup over unitaries U of |tr(UX)|, the global depolarizing channel satisfies tn(Delta_p(rho) - Delta_p(sigma)) = (1-p)*tn(rho - sigma) for equal-trace rho, sigma and p <= 1; along any history of unitaries V(i) with depolarizing rates p(i) in [0,1], tn(run rho - run sigma) = (product of (1-p(i)))*tn(rho - sigma), which is at most (1-p)^t*tn(rho - sigma) when every p(i) >= p, and (1-p)^t <= 1/(1+p*t).

name: Exact qubit form: squared Bloch distance of two noisy histories contracts by the product of squared factors
obligation: The identification of the qubit trace norm with the Bloch distance uses the cited eigenvalue fact; Python and Rust replays are exact on declared instances only.
summary: For rational Bloch vectors, noisy steps r -> (1-p)*R*r with rational rotations R (R^T R = 1) give sqDist(run r, run s) = (product of (1-p(i))^2)*sqDist(r, s), at most ((1-p)^2)^t*sqDist(r, s) when every p(i) in [p,1]; and (v.sigma)^2 = (v.v)*1 over the complex numbers, so the difference of two qubit states has both singular values |r-s|/2.

name: Conditional viability: explicit logical failure bound under fresh supply, net-efficient repair and bounded overhead
obligation: The noise recurrence is a hypothesis: independence or locality of noise, fresh ancillas, fast classical control and bounded overhead are not shown for any device; the hypotheses are only shown jointly satisfiable on declared toy numbers.
summary: If g < 1, kappa > 0, r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa), c(k) <= C, max(C,1)*p(0) < 1 and the level errors p(k) >= 0 obey p(k+1) <= c(k)*p(k)^2 whenever the backlog is bounded, then the backlog is bounded and for every L >= 0 and epsilon > 0 some level k has L*p(k) <= epsilon; with max(C,1)*p(0) <= 1/2 any k with L <= epsilon*max(C,1)*2^(2^k) works.

name: Inside the model, viability holds exactly when the fresh supply reaches threshold and the overhead means are bounded
obligation: A statement about the declared model: a failed requirement shows the certificate is empty, not that a physical machine fails.
summary: For g < 1, kappa > 0 and c(k) >= 0, the backlog is bounded and some positive physical rate has p(k) tending to zero iff r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa) and some M > 0 has amp(k) <= M^(2^k); with no supply the backlog is unbounded, with g >= 1 it is unbounded for every supply, and a tight profile p(k+1) >= c(k)*p(k)^2 with c(k) >= a*b^(2^k), b > 1, p(0) > 0 does not tend to zero.

name: Whether a physical system meets the conditional viability hypotheses is not derived
obligation: A named packet (code family, noise hypothesis, repair capacity, residual quotient) and a locality bound would be needed before any verdict; no claim about physical viability is made.
summary: Whether any physical system has noise obeying the recurrence with level-bounded overhead, a fresh ancilla supply at rate r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa) and fast classical control is not established here, in either direction; the rate comparison mu_repair >= lambda_proj at scale stays open.

name: Shared structure with the Turing-completeness branch: unbounded computation needs an unbounded supply of fresh distinguished marks
obligation: A bridge definition only: no common theorem is proved, no map between the entropy-sink supply and the blank-tape supply of the UTM branch is defined, and that branch is not part of this checkout.
summary: A fresh-mark supply is a stream of distinguished marks each usable once; a process consuming at least rmin > 0 marks per round completes at most B/rmin rounds from a total supply B, and a positive per-round consumption exhausts every finite supply; reliable quantum computation of unbounded length (QCV-Q1B, QCV-Q4) and Turing-complete computation in the parallel UTM branch each need such an unbounded supply.

name: Read token, halt outcome and terminal policy are separate carriers in a two-presentation tape-control model
obligation: State the same four facts for a general tape alphabet and head position; the content contract is chosen to separate the two presentations, so the result exhibits a split fiber and does not derive one.
summary: On the fixed carrier of two halting presentations that differ only in the scanned cell (blank or marked), a control-only report does not determine the supplied content contract, an unread report does not determine it either, one read token admits two supplied semantic adapters, and one halt outcome admits two supplied terminal policies.

name: Four-configuration transition table: one supplied contract preserved, one fails on a countertrace
obligation: Replace the enumerated carrier by an actual tape and head, and replace the contracts, which were written to produce the countertrace, by contracts stated independently of the table.
summary: In a table over the four configurations running-blank, running-marked, halted-blank and halted-marked that exposes advance, stay and halt, the supplied clean-terminal contract is preserved, the supplied marked-cell contract fails from running-marked, the identity report is adequate for the marked-cell contract, and the control-only report is not.

name: Direct finite-rule machine with total tape, first-match lookup and fuel-bounded evaluation
obligation: Relate the model to Mathlib Turing.TM0 by restricting initial tapes to finite support, splitting write-and-move rules into two steps and merging halted with stuck, then prove step simulation; no universality, extensional property or reduction is established here.
summary: A machine is a designated halt state with an ordered finite rule list over natural-number states, the symbols blank and marked, and the moves left, right and stay; a step returns halted exactly when the state is the halt state, stuck when no rule matches, and otherwise applies the first matching rule; execute iterates at most the given fuel and returns halted, stuck or fuel exhausted with the last configuration.

name: Fuel exhaustion is a typed bounded-run outcome and is not a non-halting verdict
obligation: Apply the same three-way typing to the declared-bound runs of the Genesis continuation: a run stopped at the guard or the bound stays unresolved, neither closed nor diverging, until a longer run or a proof decides it.
summary: A bounded evaluator has three terminal outcomes, halted, stuck and fuel exhausted; the fuel-exhausted outcome records only that the budget ended and is never read as divergence, and a looping fixture exhausts a budget of one step without any claim about whether it halts.

name: Finite natural-number token code for finite-rule machines with a decoder-after-encoder round trip
obligation: No converse (encoding after decoding), no source-byte format, no configuration or input encoding and no agreement between parsed code and execution is established; the token alphabet is the natural numbers, so passing to the two-symbol tape alphabet needs a prefix-code argument, since free monoids on alphabets of different sizes are not isomorphic.
summary: For every finite-rule machine, decoding the token list that encodes it (the halt-state token followed by five-token frames of state, scanned tag, next state, written tag and move tag) returns that machine, and the all-consuming decoder returns none on the empty list, a truncated frame, an invalid symbol tag and an invalid move tag in the four named fixtures.

name: Planned length-delimited request grammar and result-level agreement with the bounded evaluator
obligation: Write the module and prove the request round trip and the result-level agreement; configuration snapshots and step-by-step trace agreement remain separate obligations.
summary: The update packet plans a request code made of a fuel token, a machine-code length, one machine segment and an input word, whose code-level evaluator decodes the request and calls the bounded evaluator on the declared initial input, with seven named target theorems.

name: A no-decider boundary transports through a validity-preserving reduction and a closed decision class
obligation: Instantiate the allowed classes with ComputablePred on a code type, take the halting problem as the source predicate and prove closure under the reduction; the declaration supplies none of the three.
summary: If a map from a source predicate into proposal validity preserves the predicate exactly, and the allowed proposal deciders are closed under precomposition with that map, then a source predicate with no allowed total decider gives a proposal predicate with no allowed total decider.

name: Under a no-total-decider premise no terminalizer is closed, two-sided sound and in the allowed class
obligation: The no-total-decider premise and the class membership of the acceptance bit are hypotheses that no program carrier supplies yet; the result does not say that every terminalizer must return unresolved, and it uses three terminal values where TFQ-0330 names five.
summary: Given an allowed class with no total decider for a validity predicate, no terminalizer whose authorized bit lies in the class is both acceptance-sound and acceptance-complete, and none is acceptance-sound, rejection-sound and never unresolved; a two-valued Boolean fixture is closed, sound and complete.

name: A program carrier is admitted for an undecidability claim only with eight frozen fields
obligation: None of the eight fields is closed by the source: DTM0 and DTM1 are partial on syntax, execution and replay only, and the candidate inventory records admission as open.
summary: A program carrier is admitted for a global undecidability claim only when syntax and encodings, execution semantics, a universality witness, an extensional property, positive and negative nontriviality witnesses, an effective reduction, the split between adequacy and authorization, and replay closure are all frozen in one record.

name: Rice theorem imported for the programs of a Turing-complete language
obligation: State a local theorem that instantiates Mathlib ComputablePred.rice₂ for the chosen code language, with the semantic property and both nontriviality witnesses named, and bind it to the class-relative transport.
summary: No total computable procedure is sound and complete for a nontrivial extensional property of the programs of a Turing-complete language (Rice 1953); the source cites the theorem with its hypotheses and does not formalize it.

name: Global computability lift for an admitted carrier and a nontrivial extensional property
obligation: Choose the carrier, define the property by program behavior, give the satisfying and failing programs, prove the many-one reduction and the closure of the decision class, and cite rice₂ and halting_problem.
summary: For an admitted program carrier and a nontrivial extensional property, a total computable sound and complete authorizer would decide that property; the lift is a stated target in the source and has no local theorem.

name: Frozen blind-derivation protocol for a run from Primitive Difference toward computation
obligation: Apply the protocol to the Genesis to computability derivation and keep recovered material out of any run meant to be blind until that run is sealed.
summary: A derivation run toward computation is a proposal source: its prompt, model, tools, repository state, available context and outputs are frozen, every notion is labeled input, definition, theorem, example or open assumption, each lift carries a positive witness and a failed-descent control, and literature comparison happens only after sealing; isolation records provenance and does not show novelty or validity.

name: DTM0 finite-rule machine with total integer tape and fuel-bounded evaluator
obligation: The definition carries no input encoding, no unbounded-run semantics, no halting predicate and no comparison with Mathlib Turing.TM0; fuel exhaustion is a bounded-evaluator result and not non-halting.
summary: A DTM0 machine is a designated halt state with a finite, left-biased list of rows (state, scanned symbol, next state, written symbol, move) over the two-symbol alphabet blank and marked; a configuration is a state, an integer head and a total tape Int to symbol; execute runs at most the stated fuel and returns halted, stuck or fuelExhausted.

name: DTM0 step reports halted exactly in the designated halt state
obligation: This fixes what a declared halt means in DTM0; it is not a statement about halting of runs and selects no terminal policy.
summary: For every DTM0 machine and configuration, step returns halted exactly when the configuration's state equals the machine's halt state, and execute then returns halted at every fuel budget.

name: DTM0 write-and-halt, stuck and self-loop fixtures
obligation: The self-loop result is exhaustion of one unit of fuel; no theorem says the loop never halts, and no fixture exceeds three rows.
summary: On the three named fixtures, writeAndHaltMachine writes a mark and reaches its halt state in one transition, the empty-rule machine is stuck at its first step, and the one-row self-loop machine returns fuelExhausted with the looped configuration after one unit of fuel.

name: DTM1 List Nat token grammar for DTM0 machines
obligation: Tokens are natural numbers, not bytes; there is no configuration or input encoding and no parser-to-execution agreement.
summary: A machine code is the halt-state token followed by complete five-token frames (state, scanned tag, next state, written tag, move tag) with tags 0 and 1 for symbols and 0, 1, 2 for moves; decodeMachine consumes the whole list and returns none on an empty list, a truncated frame or an invalid tag.

name: DTM1 decode after encode recovers every DTM0 machine
obligation: Only decode after encode is stated; injectivity of decode on arbitrary lists and encode after decode are not stated.
summary: For every DTM0 machine m, decodeMachine (encodeMachine m) = some m, supported by the tag round trips decodeTapeSymbol_encodeTapeSymbol and decodeMove_encodeMove and the rule-list round trip decodeRules_encodeRules.

name: DTM1 rejects empty, truncated and invalid-tag codes
obligation: Four named inputs only; no theorem characterizes the full domain of decodeMachine.
summary: decodeMachine returns none on the four named lists [], [0,0,0,1], [0,0,2,1,0,0] and [0,0,0,1,0,3].

name: A constant receipt cannot decide a one-bit packet contract
obligation: A toy instance of the split-fibre obstruction; it says nothing about receipts in general.
summary: For the one-bit Packet type with validity equal to its bit, no function from Unit to Bool satisfies authorize (receipt p) = valid p for all p, while the identity report admits such a function.

name: Class-relative transport of a no-total-decider premise through a reduction
obligation: The allowed classes and the source no-decider premise are supplied; no computability class, halting-style source theorem or Rice reduction is instantiated.
summary: Given a map from source instances to proposals that preserves the source predicate as proposal validity, and closure of the allowed proposal deciders under precomposition with that map, a source predicate with no allowed total decider yields a proposal validity predicate with no allowed total decider.

name: Class-relative transport instantiated with Mathlib computability for halting
obligation: Halting is the only source predicate instantiated; no Rice instance, no extensional property of encoded DTM0 programs and no computable reduction from DTM0 to Nat.Partrec.Code is given.
summary: With Computable as the allowed class on both sides, a source predicate with no computable total decider and a computable validity-preserving map give proposal validity with no computable total decider; for the source predicate that program c halts on input n this is Mathlib's ComputablePred.halting_problem.

name: An acceptance-sound and acceptance-complete terminalizer yields a total decider
obligation: The no-total-decider premise and the membership of the acceptance bit in the allowed class are hypotheses; neither is discharged.
summary: For a terminalizer into authorized, rejected, unresolved that is acceptance-sound and acceptance-complete for a validity predicate, the Boolean that is true exactly on authorized decides the predicate; if that Boolean lies in an allowed class with no total decider, the terminalizer cannot be both.

name: A rejection-sound terminalizer with no unresolved case is acceptance-complete
obligation: The result leaves three options (an unsound acceptance, an unsound rejection, or an unresolved case) and does not say any of them must occur for a particular predicate.
summary: If a terminalizer never rejects a valid proposal and never returns unresolved, every valid proposal is authorized; with an allowed acceptance bit and no allowed total decider, acceptance-soundness, rejection-soundness and closure cannot all hold.

name: A closed two-sided sound terminalizer exists for the Bool predicate
obligation: A decidable one-bit predicate only; it shows closed terminalization is not forbidden without a no-decider premise.
summary: On Bool with validity equal to the bit, the terminalizer sending true to authorized and false to rejected is acceptance-sound, acceptance-complete, rejection-sound and closed.

name: Control-only and unread reports cannot decide the tape-control content contract
obligation: The contract and adapters are supplied examples; the model is not the full Turing-machine model.
summary: In the tape-control model with cells blank and marked and outcomes advance, stay, halt, no function of the control outcome and no function of the always-unread report equals contentContract on every presentation, and the read token blank is given opposite verdicts by the two supplied semantic adapters.

name: A syntactic halt or verified outcome does not select a terminal policy
obligation: Existence of two policies only; no policy is selected or justified.
summary: In the DTM0 model, the tape-control model and the replay model, a halted or verified outcome receives different terminal values from two supplied policies: acceptHalted versus leaveAllOpen, acceptHalt versus rejectAll, and authorizeOnVerified versus leaveVerifiedOpen.

name: Four-configuration table: one preserved contract and one violated contract
obligation: Two supplied Boolean contracts on one finite table; nothing is said about transition systems in general.
summary: The four-configuration transition table maps every configuration to one that cleanTerminalContract accepts, so it preserves that contract, and it does not preserve markedCellContract because runningMarked is accepted while its successor runningBlank is not.

name: Full-configuration report is adequate for the marked-cell contract; the control report is not
obligation: A finite adequacy example; whether any report is adequate for a semantic property of arbitrary programs is not addressed.
summary: On the four configurations the identity report is adequate for markedCellContract, whereas the control-outcome report is not, because haltedBlank and haltedMarked both report stay and the contract separates them, so no function of the control outcome decides the contract.

name: Replay succeeds only on the submission bound in the receipt
obligation: Equality is structural equality of a finite record, not a digest; verifier soundness and custody are not modelled.
summary: In the finite structural replay model, if replay of a receipt on an observed submission returns replayed with some outcome, then the observed submission equals the submission bound in the receipt.

name: Finite replay model rejects self-pass and substituted checker, contract and schema
obligation: Six rfl facts on five named submissions; the model does not prove that every substitution is caught.
summary: Under authorizeTrueRoot, verify returns contractRejected for the invalid submission that sets selfPass, returns bindingRejected for the checker, contract-version and schema-version substitutions, issues a receipt that replays the valid submission as verified, and rejects the invalid payload as a substitution.

name: Site labels: co-location is enough and separation is not
obligation: Site is an unused finite label; the statement carries no custody, security or independence content.
summary: For the presentation with identity report and equal source and evaluator sites, a report-only authorization exists; for the presentation with a Unit report and distinct sites, none exists.

name: Two authorization extensions over one Bool primitive-difference analogue
obligation: The analogue is not the J011 interface and no naturality statement about all primitive differences follows.
summary: Over the minimal Bool analogue of a primitive difference with two unequal marks, identityExtension and rejectingExtension give different validity and terminal values at the same carrier point.

name: Primitive-difference quotient report cannot decide a ZeroRel-splitting validity
obligation: Not built here: the file imports J011_minimal_publication, whose source is absent from this repository, so the recorded proof is unreplayed.
summary: For a primitive difference P and a Bool validity that differs on some ZeroRel P class, no function on the canonical quotient report pdProj P agrees with validity everywhere; a ZeroRel-constant validity has a quotient decision.

name: SHA-256 replay packet for the four-configuration table (Python port)
obligation: Evaluator correspondence to the Lean model, SHA-256 collision resistance, runtime integrity and custody remain assumptions; the PowerShell runtime pin is not reproduced and the formal replay uses Lean v4.35.0 instead of the recorded v4.32.2.
summary: A manifest binding eight artifacts by SHA-256 together with a four-row transition proposal, a contract and a leave-open policy verifies under the Python port; it finds the clean-terminal contract preserved, the marked-cell contract violated at runningMarked and haltedMarked, the control-outcome report inadequate (haltedBlank and haltedMarked share stay), the route open_due_to_inadequate_report and the terminal open, and refuses 21 tamper mutations.

name: No computability carrier is admitted for the authorization lift
obligation: A carrier with syntax, execution, simulation, an extensional property with encoded witnesses, an effective reduction and a replay boundary must be frozen before any Rice-style claim.
summary: The recovered candidate record stays globally open: for AIT-DTM0 only syntax, execution semantics, adequacy and replay closure are partial and universality, extensionality, nontriviality and effective reduction are open, and PO-022, PO-023 and AIT-PACKET4 are open; the validator refuses any selection or admission.

name: Rice, Goedel and the LLM corollary are not formalized in the recovered files
obligation: Instantiate the transport for a nontrivial extensional property of encoded programs with Mathlib's ComputablePred.rice and a computable reduction from the DTM0 carrier before any such claim.
summary: No recovered declaration states Rice's theorem, a halting-problem reduction, Goedel's second incompleteness theorem or the LLM corollary; the only link toward them is the class-relative transport with a supplied no-decider premise, which the recovery-time MathlibBridge file instantiates for halting only.

name: DTM0 is not shown Turing-complete and has no universality theorem
obligation: A faithful comparison needs a finite-support tape restriction, the stay move split into Mathlib's move-or-write statements, and a halting predicate such as exists fuel with execute returning halted.
summary: DTM0 has no simulation theorem, no machine that runs encoded machines, no input or configuration encoding, no parser-to-execution agreement and no equivalence with Mathlib's Turing.TM0 or with Nat.Partrec.Code; its fuel-bounded evaluator decides only bounded runs.

name: Deutsch 2013: laws as statements about possible and unachievable tasks
obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1210.7439; nothing in the paper is used as a premise of any repository result.
summary: Deutsch (2013, arXiv:1210.7439, Section 1.1 eqs. (1)-(2) pp. 2-4 and Section 1.2 p. 5) proposes to state physical laws as statements about which physical transformations (tasks) can be caused to happen and which cannot, in place of dynamical laws plus initial conditions, together with the composition principle (Section 1.2 p. 5), computation media (Section 2.6 eq. (9) pp. 13-14) and Einstein locality on composite substrates (Section 3.10 p. 33). This node records the proposal as published.

name: Imported vocabulary: task, constructor, possible and not possible
obligation: Taking the possible and not-possible partition of tasks as primitive is a different foundational choice from the repository's admitted primitive PG-ROOT-DIFF-STRUCTURE and its replayed refusal predicates. No source derives either from the other.
summary: Imported vocabulary, audited against Deutsch (2013, Section 1.1 eqs. (1)-(2) pp. 2-4) and Deutsch-Marletto (2015, Section 2 pp. 6-8): a task is a set of ordered input/output attribute pairs of a substrate; a constructor causes the transformation and retains its ability to do so again; a task is possible when the laws of nature impose no limit short of perfection on how accurately it can be performed and how well a constructor can retain its ability to perform it again, and not possible otherwise; Principle I (Section 2 p. 8) states that the state of a composite substrate S1 + S2 is the pair of states on S1 and S2 and a construction on S1 changes only the S1 state. The repository uses none of this vocabulary as a primitive.

name: Analogy: Genesis separation task versus a not-possible task
obligation: No source maps cost-bounded response search to constructor existence. The Genesis statement stays within its declared candidate list; it is not a statement about all constructors.
summary: Open question: whether the Genesis finite statement that, among the 111 declared candidate sequences, no response of cost below 2 separates the collapsed pair (PG-GEN-COLLAPSE-AND-FIRST-SEPARATION, as narrowed by its PFP review) is a finite instance of a constructor-theoretic statement that a task is not possible. Common ground: both sort proposed changes of a finite system into available and refused by a rule on the system. Differences: the Genesis statement quantifies over a declared candidate list and a cost, has no constructor and no accuracy limit, and concerns regime augmentation, not physical transformation. Only an analogy is established.

name: Analogy: obstructed change and off-image refusal versus a not-possible task
obligation: The repository predicates are decided by the structure of the attempted change; the imported notion is decided by what a constructor could do. A bridge would need a model of constructors on the Genesis regime.
summary: Open question: whether the proved Genesis statement that an attempted change is obstructed exactly when it adds an xrx or identifies two related terms (PG-GEN-ONGOING-OBSTRUCTION), and the S(n) off-image refusal (PG-SN-OFF-IMAGE-REFUSAL), are finite instances of a not-possible task. Both are decidable refusal predicates on a finite model. The source notion of a not-possible task concerns the existence of a constructor with arbitrary accuracy, which neither predicate mentions. Only an analogy is established.

name: Finite target: distinguishable attributes and report fibers
obligation: Checked in Lean 4 on Finset for all finite carriers and by the exhaustive check for |X|<=4, |R|<=3. Whether the finite condition deserves the name "distinguishable attributes" in the source's sense depends on the imported definition, which this repository does not adopt.
summary: Formalized finite statement. For a finite set X and a report map q from X to R, two attributes A and B of X (nonemptiness is not needed) are separated by a deterministic task, meaning a function f from R to {0,1} with f(q(a))=0 on A and f(q(b))=1 on B, if and only if q(A) and q(B) are disjoint. Checked in Lean 4 over Finset for arbitrary types X and R with decidable equality on R: both directions and the biconditional; when q(A) and q(B) are disjoint the indicator of B on the union of A and B is constant on the fibers of q (HistoryReport.FiberConstant, the form PG-HISTORY-REPORT-CRITERION takes); and an exhaustive bitmask decision check over all (q, A, B) with nonempty attributes for 1<=|X|<=4 and 1<=|R|<=3. This matches the constructor-theoretic notion of distinguishable attributes only on its deterministic finite fragment: accuracy, repeatability and constructor existence are not modelled.

name: Deutsch and Marletto 2015: constructor theory of information
obligation: Record only. Full text of arXiv:1405.5563 audited on 2026-10-22; its postulates are not adopted as repository primitives.
summary: Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563) formulate a constructor theory of information by defining computation variables (Section 3 p. 9), clonable variables and information media (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10) prior to distinguishability (Section 5 eq. (4) p. 11), avoiding the circularity of Section 1 eq. (1) p. 3. Section 7 (p. 20) and Section 8 (pp. 20-24) define superinformation media and derive non-distinguishability, no-cloning of non-orthogonal states, complementarity and unpredictability from Principles I-IX. This node records the paper as published.

name: Imported: information media and the interoperability principle
obligation: The interoperability principle (Principle III, Section 6 p. 12) constrains composite information variables to include S1 x S2 in the source's framework. It is not shown to select the Hilbert tensor product, local tomography or any positive cone, so it does not discharge FQ-GAP-TENSOR-UNIQUENESS.
summary: Imported principles, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Sections 3-6 pp. 9-12): a computation variable is a set S of at least two possible attributes for which all permutation tasks are possible with side-effects (Section 3 p. 9); a variable S is clonable if the cloning task R_S(x0) = union_{x in S} {(x, x0) -> (x, x)} is possible with side-effects for some preparable blank attribute x0 (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10); an information variable is a clonable computation variable, and an information medium is a substrate with at least one information variable (Section 4 p. 10). Distinguishability is defined afterward in Section 5 (eq. (4) p. 11) by mapping into an information variable, avoiding circularity, and every information variable is then shown to be distinguishable. Principle III (interoperability, Section 6 p. 12) states that the composite S1 + S2 of two substrates with information variables S1 and S2 is an information medium with information variable S1 x S2.

name: Imported: superinformation medium
obligation: The definition (Section 7 p. 20) is an assumption of this branch. Whether the repository's declared finite quantum interface meets its finite cloning shadow is the content of CT-QUBIT-NO-CLONING-FINITE-TARGET, which is checked in Lean only in the narrowed form recorded there (explicit clone maps, the Z-union-X obstruction for additive maps, the pairwise equal-or-orthogonal classification); the fidelity argument and complete positivity are not formalised.
summary: Imported definition, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Section 6 pp. 14-18 and Section 7 p. 20): an information observable is an information variable X whose attributes satisfy double-complement closure x = u_x under distinguishability (Section 6, Principle VIII p. 16); a superinformation medium is an information medium with at least two information observables X and Y that contain only mutually disjoint attributes and whose union X union Y is not an information observable (Section 7 p. 20). Sections 8.1 and 8.3 (pp. 20-22) show under Principles III, IV, VI, VII, VIII and IX that X union Y is neither distinguishable nor clonable. The repository neither adopts this definition as a primitive nor claims that its finite carriers satisfy Principles I-IX.

name: Source claim: superinformation media yield no-cloning and complementarity
obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1405.5563 Sections 8.1-8.7; the finite qubit target checks only the Pauli-eigenstate cloning statement over Q(i).
summary: Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Sections 8.1-8.7 pp. 20-25) derive within their postulate system (Principles I-IX) that in any superinformation medium: (i) the union X union Y of two subsidiary information observables is not distinguishable (Section 8.1 p. 20); (ii) no observable has refinements of both X and Y (complementarity, Section 8.2 p. 21); (iii) X union Y is not clonable (Section 8.3 p. 22); and (iv) composite superinformation media can hold locally inaccessible information (entanglement, Section 8.7 pp. 24-25). This node records those source claims; the finite qubit target of this stage checks only the linear-algebraic cloning statement for the six Pauli eigenstates over Q(i).

name: Finite target: cloneable and non-cloneable attributes of a qubit
obligation: Not proved in Lean: complete positivity of cloneZ, cloneX and cloneY, and trace preservation of cloneX and cloneY (only cloneZ is shown trace-preserving); that completely positive trace-preserving maps cannot decrease fidelity (x <= x^2 is a hypothesis of the arithmetic lemma, not derived); and the equivalence of the semantic notion "some CPTP map clones every state of the subset" with "pairwise equal or orthogonal" in either direction (the Lean classification takes the latter as the definition of cloneable). The link to the imported definition of a superinformation medium is a reading of definitions.
summary: Finite statement over Q(i), checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. Take the qubit with the six Pauli eigenstates as rays. (a) The explicit measure-and-prepare maps cloneZ, cloneX and cloneY (rho to the mixture of the two basis clones with weights Tr(P rho)) send each of |0>,|1>; |+>,|->; |+i>,|-i> to its own clone rho tensor rho; cloneZ is shown trace-preserving. (b) The exact relation |0><0|+|1><1| = |+><+|+|-><-| holds in Herm(2), and the difference of the two clone sums has entry -1/2 on |00><11| and |11><00|, so no additive map (hence no linear map) clones all four of |0>,|1>,|+>,|->. (c) The exact squared overlaps of the six states are 1 (equal), 0 (antipodal) or 1/2 (otherwise); for a rational x in [0,1], x <= x^2 forces x in {0,1}; and an exhaustive count over the 64 subsets of the six states shows that exactly 10 subsets are pairwise equal-or-orthogonal (the empty set, 6 singletons and 3 antipodal pairs) and that the maximal such subsets are the three antipodal pairs. In Lean "cloneable subset" in (c) is defined as pairwise equal-or-orthogonal.

name: Marletto 2016: constructor theory of probability
obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1507.03287 Sections 4-7; its decision-theoretic premises (T1-T2, R1-R4, A1-A2) are distinct from the frame-function hypotheses of GP-IMPORT-GLEASON.
summary: Marletto (2016, arXiv:1507.03287) formulates unpredictability in superinformation media via the non-existence of an X-predictor constructor (Section 4 pp. 21-22), defines X-indistinguishability equivalence classes and X-partitions of unity [f(z)_x] through the limiting ensemble fraction constructor D_x^(N) under conditions E1-E2 (Section 5 pp. 23-29), and shows that in a decision-supporting superinformation theory (conditions T1-T2 and R1-R4, Table 1 p. 32) a player automaton Gamma satisfying decision axioms A1-A2 (Section 6.2 pp. 35-36) values an X-game of chance G_X(y) by the additive expectation V{G_X(y)} = sum_{x in X} f(y)_x x (Section 7 eqs. (16), (18), (20) pp. 41-47). This node records the paper's results.

name: Marletto 2016: constructor theory of thermodynamics
obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1608.02625 Sections 5-7; the repository has no thermodynamic substrate or adiabatic-accessibility relation.
summary: Marletto (2016, v5 2017, arXiv:1608.02625) defines work media as substrates with at least three equally-spaced energy attributes admitting an adjacent-pair swap on two replicas (so work variables are information variables by Principle VII, Section 5 pp. 27-31), states the First Law as interoperability of work media (Law I, eq. (4) p. 32), and defines adiabatic possibility {x -> y} as possibility with side-effects on work variables only (Section 5.3 p. 33). Section 6 (pp. 34-42) defines heat media, Principle IX (interoperability of heat media, p. 38), the Second Law (Law II, p. 39: existence of heat attributes h1, h2 with {h1 -> h2} adiabatically possible and {h2 -> h1} not adiabatically possible), an entropy function via the adiabatic 'is-like' relation (pp. 39-41), and the Zeroth Law (Law X, p. 42), deriving Kelvin's statement in Section 7 (pp. 42-44). This node records the paper's results.

name: Marletto-Vedral and Bose et al. 2017: gravitationally mediated entanglement witness
obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1707.06036 and arXiv:1707.06050; the repository makes no physical claim about gravity.
summary: Marletto and Vedral (2017, arXiv:1707.06036, pp. 1-4, Fig. 1) argue within constructor theory that if a mediator M locally couples two quantum systems Q1 and Q2 (via Q1 <-> M <-> Q2 with no direct Q1-Q2 coupling) and generates entanglement from a product state, then M must carry at least two incompatible observables (a superinformation medium), and propose testing gravitationally induced phases between two interferometric masses; Bose et al. (2017, arXiv:1707.06050, pp. 1-5, eqs. (1)-(8)) independently propose a spin-correlation entanglement witness W = |(sigma_x^(1) tensor sigma_z^(2)) + (sigma_y^(1) tensor sigma_y^(2))| > 1 (eq. (8) p. 4) for two Stern-Gerlach interferometers interacting through Newtonian gravity phases delta phi_+- and delta phi_-+ (eqs. (2)-(4) p. 2). This node records both papers; no experiment is claimed to have been performed.

name: Imported inference: entanglement through a mediator indicates a non-classical mediator
obligation: The inference (arXiv:1707.06036 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1707.06050 pp. 1-2) is an assumption of this branch. It does not use or support any repository Lean result.
summary: Imported inference, audited against Marletto-Vedral (2017, arXiv:1707.06036, pp. 2-3) and Bose et al. (2017, arXiv:1707.06050, pp. 1-2): if two quantum systems Q1 and Q2 start in a separable state, interact only locally through a mediating system M (Q1 <-> M and M <-> Q2, with no direct Q1-Q2 interaction, Principle I locality), and end in an entangled state of Q1 + Q2, then M cannot be a classical medium (in Marletto-Vedral, M must have at least two disjoint incompatible observables whose union is not an information variable; in Bose et al., any mediator modeled by local operations and classical communication cannot create entanglement). The repository has no gravity model; TFQ-0084 is a finite shadow only.

name: Finite target: a phase interaction entangles; local operations do not
obligation: Statement (d), an exact separating functional on the 4x4 density matrix relative to the product family in the form of DS-QM071, is not proved. The Lean module defines schmidtWitnessExpectation(M) = |det M|^2, a quadratic function of the amplitude matrix that vanishes on product vectors and is positive on psi_u for u != 1; that is a restatement of (a), not a linear functional on density matrices, and it is not shown to vanish on mixtures of product states or tied to DS-QM071. The rank inequality rank(A M B^T) <= rank(M) for general rank is stated only through the 2x2 determinant identity (preservation of det M = 0). No physical claim is attached.
summary: Finite statement over Q(i), checked in Lean 4 for (a) to (c); (d) is not proved. For u in Q(i) (the Lean proofs of (a) and (b) do not use |u|=1), the two-qubit vector psi_u = (1,1,1,u)/2 has coefficient matrix M_u = [[1,1],[1,u]]/2 of determinant (u-1)/4. (a) psi_u is a product vector if and only if u=1. (b) The squared concurrence, defined as 4|det M|^2, equals |u-1|^2/4 for M_u; for u=(3+4i)/5, where |u|=1, it equals 1/5. (c) For all 2x2 matrices A and B over Q(i), det(A M B^T) = det(A) det(M) det(B), so det M = 0 implies det(A M B^T) = 0: local operations cannot raise a product vector to Schmidt rank 2; and diag(1,1,1,u) applied to the product vector (1,1,1,1)/2 gives psi_u. The physical inference from such entanglement to a non-classical mediator is imported, not part of this target.

name: Finite strict posets and spacelike separation in CausalOrder.lean
obligation: The theorem name incomparability_not_transitive_c1 overstates its statement. A genuine non-transitive example (the four-element N poset) is part of the finite net target of this stage.
summary: lean4/CausalOrder.lean defines FiniteStrictPoset n (an irreflexive transitive relation on Fin n) and spacelike separation (x differs from y and neither precedes the other). It establishes spacelike_symm and spacelike_irrefl; on the named examples C1 (0<1, 0<2) and C2 (the four-element diamond) it establishes c1_spacelike_1_2, c2_causal_0_3, order_independence_witness (C1 and its dual differ) and the table entries c1_mu_spacelike_vanishes and c2_mu_top_bottom (value 1). Scope: three decided examples, no general causal-set theory. The theorem named incomparability_not_transitive_c1 states only that e1 and e2 are spacelike in both orders and that e1 is not spacelike to itself; it does not exhibit a failure of transitivity of spacelike separation. The table c2_mu is checked entry by entry; the Lean file does not state the Mobius recursion for it.

name: Product tables are no-signalling in NoSignallingCore.lean
obligation: The quantum statement that commuting local measurements at spacelike separated points give setting-independent marginals is not stated in this file.
summary: lean4/NoSignallingCore.lean establishes, for natural-number-valued tables of the product form P x y a b = PA x a * PB y b in which each PB y sums to 1 over a listed outcome set, that the marginal on the first party does not depend on the second party's setting (product_noSignalling, marginalA_product), and that the table sig, in which the first outcome equals the second setting, has a setting-dependent marginal, so NoSignallingBA fails (sig_signals). Scope: product tables over the naturals with outcome lists; no quantum states, no commuting local observables, no relation to the posets of CausalOrder.lean.

name: Haag and Kastler 1964: local nets of observable algebras
obligation: Record only. The checkout holds no copy of the 1964 print article; the standard postulate list is checked in secondary sources (arXiv:math-ph/9903028 Section 1 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1607.03901 Section 6 pp. 28-30), while the primary 1964 numbering remains to be audited against the print text.
summary: Haag and Kastler (1964) formulate quantum field theory through a net that assigns to bounded spacetime regions the algebras of observables localized there, with the standard structural requirements later grouped as isotony (larger regions have larger algebras), locality (algebras of spacelike separated regions commute) and Poincare covariance, and with states as positive functionals. This node records the framework; the paper's own list of postulates is not reproduced.

name: Imported: a causal spacetime with a net of local algebras
obligation: The counts and products are one supplied four-point order and four supplied integer matrices. They are not a net indexed by continuum regions and not a Minkowski light cone. The Haag-Kastler import and the external light-cone lift named by DS-QM033-064-074-083-QHELD-CONTINUUM stay open. CausalOrder.lean is not a premise of a continuum theorem in this record.
summary: On the four-point strict order with the ordered relations 0<2, 1<2 and 1<3, the scan of all 64 triples holds, no point is related to itself, there are exactly 3 ordered relations, and exactly 3 of the 6 unordered pairs are spacelike: {0,1}, {0,3} and {2,3}. For the integer matrices A=[[1,2],[3,4]], B=[[5,6],[7,8]], X=[[0,1],[1,0]] and Z=[[1,0],[0,-1]], both (A tensor I)(I tensor B) and (I tensor B)(A tensor I) equal A tensor B, whose sixteen entries sum to 260. The products (X tensor I)(Z tensor I) and (Z tensor I)(X tensor I) differ, their (0,2) entries are -1 and 1, and XZ+ZX is the zero matrix. The determinants are det A = -2, det B = -2, det X = -1 and det Z = -1. A net of unital star-algebras indexed by continuum regions, and a Minkowski light cone, stay imported. This record does not import CausalOrder.lean and does not transport these finite counts to a continuum net.

name: Finite target: isotony and locality for a net on a finite poset
obligation: Not proved in Lean: the statements for the full local matrix algebras A(O) (linear spans of elementary tensors, for example 2^|O| x 2^|O| matrices): that commutation of elementary tensors extends by bilinearity to the algebras and that A(O1) is a subalgebra of A(O2) as matrix algebras; the single-site monoid M is generic and is not instantiated at 2x2 matrices. The net is kinematical: dynamics, a time-slice property and covariance are not modelled, so the statement is the finite shadow of two axioms and nothing more.
summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 for site-factorized operators. For a FiniteStrictPoset P on n points put one qubit (a single-site monoid M) at each point; an operator A : Fin n -> M is localized in a subset O of P when it is the identity outside O, so the Lean "algebra" of O is the set of elementary tensor operators localized in O, not the full matrix algebra on the qubits in O. (a) Isotony: O1 inside O2 and A localized in O1 imply A localized in O2. (b) Locality: if every point of O1 is spacelike to every point of O2, then O1 and O2 are disjoint and operators localized in O1 and in O2 commute under the sitewise product. (c) The spacelike relation of CausalOrder.lean is symmetric (spacelike_symm) and irreflexive (spacelike_irrefl) and not transitive: on the four-element N poset 0<2, 1<2, 1<3, points 1 and 0 are spacelike, 0 and 3 are spacelike, and 1<3 are related. The content of Haag-Kastler locality (commutation forced by causal separation of dynamics) is absent because this net has no dynamics.

name: Reeh and Schlieder 1961: cyclicity of the vacuum
obligation: Record only. The precise hypotheses (spectrum condition, vacuum uniqueness, covariance) are to be audited against the paper.
summary: Reeh and Schlieder (1961) study the unitary equivalence of Lorentz-invariant fields and obtain what is cited as the Reeh-Schlieder property: for a positive-energy, Poincare covariant theory with a vacuum vector, the vacuum is cyclic for the algebra of any bounded open region. The paper is in German and the checkout holds no copy; the statement and hypotheses are recorded from citations.

name: Imported: Reeh-Schlieder property and its continuum hypotheses
obligation: The inputs of the property are the continuum Hilbert lift and the Stone theorem, which the repository records as open. The gap route below lists them.
summary: Imported property: in a net of local algebras on Minkowski space with a translation action whose generators have positive spectrum (spectrum condition) and a vacuum vector, the vacuum is cyclic for every local algebra, and under further hypotheses separating for the algebra of a region with spacelike complement. The proof uses analytic continuation of translations, hence a continuous translation group and its generator (Stone theorem) on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Both are open nodes of the repository. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/algebraic components and non-equivalence fences: (1) over any semiring R and for any dimensions dA, dB (even when dA < dB), if Fin dA is inhabited then CyclicForA Omega implies SeparatingForAc Omega via matrix associativity (X * Omega) * Y = X * (Omega * Y), so any nonzero right-kernel vector or identically zero column precludes cyclicity even when dA < dB; (2) discharging the open finite items of TFQ-2107, none of |000>, |GHZ_3>, or |W_3> is cyclic on any single site (s in {0, 1, 2}), |000> has neither a left inverse nor cyclicity on any pair of sites while |GHZ_3> and |W_3> are both cyclic and separating on every pair of sites, all three states have full complementary rank 1 and are cyclic on the full 3-site algebra, and across the 4-qubit 2+2 bipartition neither |0000> nor |GHZ_4> is cyclic whereas the 2-Bell-pair cluster state has full complementary rank 4 and is both cyclic and separating; and (3) on a finite N-site ring, cyclicShift N aliases with period N, translation-invariant constant vectors have zero discrete momentum difference, and the translation-invariant 3-qubit product vacuum |000> fails cyclicity on every proper subsystem.

name: Finite target: cyclicity of a state for a subsystem algebra is a rank condition
obligation: Not proved in Lean: separating implies full column rank (so the three-way equivalence is not complete); the identification of full column rank with full rank of the reduced state; the qubit subset bookkeeping; the conclusion "not cyclic" for the single-site cases (cyclic implies left inverse is proved only for dB <= dA, and a single site has dA=2 < dB=4; the kernel vectors give non-separating only) and for |000> on pairs (a zero column is exhibited but "zero column implies no left inverse implies not cyclic" is not stated as a theorem); that |000> is cyclic for the full algebra. A Lean proof of the equivalence for general n is open. The relation to the continuum theorem is an analogy: finite dimension has no translation group or spectrum condition.
summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. Let Omega be a dA x dB matrix over a semiring R (the amplitude matrix of a vector in H_A tensor H_{A^c}; for qubits dA = 2^|A| and dB = 2^|A^c|, but the qubit tensor-factor bookkeeping is not formalised). Omega is cyclic for End(H_A) when every dA x dB matrix is X Omega for some X. (a) If Omega has a left inverse L with L Omega = I_dB (full column rank dB, which over a field is full rank of the reduced state on A^c) then Omega is cyclic and Omega is separating for End(H_{A^c}) (Omega Y = 0 implies Y = 0). (b) Conversely, cyclic implies a left inverse whenever dB <= dA (an injection Fin dB -> Fin dA is supplied). (c) A nonzero vector in the right kernel of Omega makes Omega not separating. (d) Exact 3-qubit instances over Z for the product vector |000>, GHZ = |000>+|111> and W = |100>+|010>+|001>: explicit nonzero right-kernel vectors for every single-site unfolding (2 x 4), explicit integer left inverses of every pair-of-sites unfolding (4 x 2) for GHZ and W, and a zero column in every pair-of-sites unfolding of |000>.

name: Epstein and Glaser 1973: the role of locality in perturbation theory
obligation: Record only. Audited against the Numdam full text (AIHPA_1973__19_3_211_0); nothing in the paper is used as a premise of a repository theorem.
summary: Epstein and Glaser (1973, Ann. Inst. H. Poincare A 19, 211-295, Abstract p. 211, Section 1.1 pp. 214-215, Section 2.1 eq. (9) p. 218, Section 2.2 eq. (30) p. 223, and Section 5 pp. 231-237) give an inductive construction of the perturbation series S(g) = 1 + sum_{n>=1} (i^n / n!) int T_n(x_1,...,x_n) g(x_1)...g(x_n) dx in which each order T_n is constructed from lower orders by causal factorization outside the total diagonal and by splitting causal distributions with scaling degree bounds on the diagonal. This node records the paper as published.

name: Imported: causal factorization of the scattering matrix
obligation: Audited against Epstein-Glaser (1973) eqs. (9), (30) and Brunetti-Fredenhagen (2000) eq. (2) and Condition P3. The continuum distribution extension has no counterpart in the repository's finite posets.
summary: Imported property, audited and corrected against Epstein and Glaser (1973, Section 1.1 condition (C.A.) pp. 214-215, Section 2.1 condition (Caus. 1) eq. (9) p. 218, Section 2.2 eq. (30) p. 223) and Brunetti and Fredenhagen (2000, arXiv:math-ph/9903028, Section 1 eq. (2) p. 4 and Section 3 Condition P3 p. 15): the scattering operator satisfies V(g, h1+h2) = S(g)^{-1} S(g+h1+h2) = V(g, h1) V(g, h2) (and at g=0, S(g1+g2) = S(g1) S(g2)) whenever supp h1 does not intersect the causal past of supp h2, written supp h1 cap (supp h2 + V^-) = empty (which includes spacelike separation as well as causal future separation, not only supp h1 inside the causal future of supp h2). Equivalently at each order n, the time-ordered operator-valued distributions factorize as T(P union Q) = T(P) T(Q) whenever {x_i : i in P} cap ({x_j : j in Q} + V^-) = empty (eq. (30) p. 223; Condition P3 p. 15), and renormalization reduces to extending time-ordered products across the total diagonal. The repository has neither operator-valued distributions nor a continuum Minkowski causal cone. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/algebraic components and non-equivalence fences: (1) over any group G and additive coupling carrier A, the relative Bogoliubov operator bogoliubovV S g h = (S g)^{-1} * S(g + h) satisfies V(g, 0) = 1, the unconditional telescoping cocycle law V(g, h1) * V(g + h1, h2) = V(g, h1 + h2), and the equivalence V(g, h1 + h2) = V(g, h1) * V(g, h2) <-> V(g + h1, h2) = V(g, h2), while on the diamond poset C2 the Epstein-Glaser separation predicate noInCausalPast C2 holds symmetrically for spacelike ([d1], [d2]) and one-way for future-before-past ([d1, d2, d3], [d0]); (2) on the 4-element N poset (0 < 2, 1 < 2, 1 < 3), all 5 linear extensions extN0..extN4 are connected by chains of adjacent spacelike swaps (SpacelikeSwapChain posetN) and have identical ordered products for every spacelike-commuting monoid assignment (discharging the finite-poset connectivity question of TFQ-2110), while anticommuting Pauli operators X, Z on (n0, n3) flip the sign between extN3 and extN4; and (3) coincident pairs (x, x) on a FiniteStrictPoset are never spacelike separated, the 4D Epstein-Glaser polynomial counterterm dimension binom(omega + 4, 4) equals (1, 5, 15, 35, 70) for omega = 0..4, and off-diagonal factorization (x != y) leaves coincident-diagonal contact counterterms c unconstrained.

name: Finite target: time-ordered products over linear extensions of a poset
obligation: Not proved in Lean: that any two linear extensions of an arbitrary finite strict poset are connected by a chain of adjacent spacelike swaps, which is the step that turns swap invariance into independence from the choice of linear extension. Connectivity is exhibited for the two extensions of C2 only; for the N poset the five extensions are counted but their connectivity, and hence the equality of their ordered products, is not stated. The relation to Epstein-Glaser is an analogy.
summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. For a FiniteStrictPoset P and elements A_x (x in P) of a monoid with A_x A_y = A_y A_x for all spacelike pairs x,y: the ordered product along a listing of P is unchanged by one adjacent swap of spacelike elements, hence by any chain of adjacent spacelike swaps. Exact checks: the diamond C2 has exactly 2 linear extensions among the 24 permutations of its four points, [0,1,2,3] and [0,2,1,3], connected by one adjacent spacelike swap of 1 and 2; the N poset has exactly 5 linear extensions; with integer 2x2 Pauli matrices on C2 the two ordered products agree when the spacelike points 1 and 2 carry the commuting matrices Z and Z, and differ by the sign -1 (and are unequal) when they carry the anticommuting matrices X and Z. The distribution extension and the ultraviolet content of the Epstein-Glaser construction have no finite counterpart.

name: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin 1987: space-time as a causal set
obligation: Record only. Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 3 p. 6) and Reid (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section II p. 2) were audited in full; the 1987 PRL print article is not held in the checkout.
summary: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin (1987) propose that spacetime at the smallest scales is a discrete structure, a causal set: a locally finite set with a partial order encoding past and future. They examine how a Lorentzian manifold can approximate such a set, note that effective dimensionality can vary with length scale, and sketch a quantum dynamics. Sorkin's Valdivia notes (2003) are a later survey. This node records the proposal.

name: A finite causal set is a FiniteStrictPoset
obligation: Definitional only. Nothing about manifold-likeness, dimension or the continuum limit is asserted.
summary: Reading of definitions. A causal set in the sense of the source is a locally finite partially ordered set; in the strict-order form its relation is irreflexive and transitive, and local finiteness is automatic on a finite set. This is the structure FiniteStrictPoset n of lean4/CausalOrder.lean. The Python class CausalSet in code/python/src/general_relativity/causal_set.py builds a poset from relations, takes the transitive closure and refuses cycles. The identification involves no sprinkling, no embedding in a Lorentzian manifold and no dynamics.

name: Finite target: ordering fraction, Myrheim-Meyer dimension and Hasse diagrams as exact rationals
obligation: Not proved in Lean: that the n x n grid poset (a FiniteStrictPoset on n^2 points) has R(n) strictly related pairs, so (i) is arithmetic on a posited count cross-checked against the diamond only at n=2; the derivation of f(d) from the Gamma-function formula; correctness of the nearest-dimension selector beyond the six listed inputs; that the Hasse relation itself generates the order and is the minimal such relation. Everything is rational arithmetic on named finite posets. The dimension estimator is a heuristic for sprinklings; the finite estimate on a small poset carries no manifold statement.
summary: Finite statement, checked in Lean 4 in the following narrowed form. The ordering fraction of a finite causal set is the exact rational r = 2R/(n(n-1)), with R the number of strictly related pairs (CausalSet.ordering_fraction); Lean computes r(C1)=2/3 and r(C2)=5/6 from the relation tables of CausalOrder.lean. In Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 7 p. 16), the expected ordering fraction of a Poisson sprinkling into a d-dimensional Minkowski causal interval normalized by binom(N,2) is f(d) = (3/2) Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2 + 1) / Gamma(3d/2 + 1) = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (2 Gamma(3d/2)) (in Reid 2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section III eq. (5) p. 5, normalizing by <N>^2 instead of binom(N,2) gives f(d)/2 = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (4 Gamma(3d/2))), with exact rational values f(1)=1, f(2)=1/2, f(3)=8/35 and f(4)=1/10; in Lean these four values are entered as a table (70 f(d) = 70, 35, 16, 7) and not derived from the Gamma formula. (i) If the n x n grid with the componentwise product order has R(n) = (n(n+1)/2)^2 - n^2 strictly related pairs (a count entered as a definition in Lean, not derived from a poset), then 4 R(n) = n^2 (n-1)(n+3), the ordering fraction is r = (n+3)/(2(n+1)) for all n >= 2 with r(n) - 1/2 = 1/(n+1), the values for n=2..6 are 5/6, 3/4, 7/10, 2/3, 9/14, and r(2) = 5/6 equals the exactly computed r(C2) of the diamond. This is an observation about a lattice, not an instance of the sprinkling theorem. (ii) An exact nearest-dimension selector over d in {1,2,3,4} with tie reporting is defined and checked on the six inputs 5/6, 3/4, 7/10, 1/2, 8/35, 1/10, giving [1], [1,2] (an exact tie), [2], [2], [3], [4]. (iii) The Hasse covering relation of any FiniteStrictPoset is contained in every subrelation E of the order such that every related pair is in E or has an intermediate element (one half of "unique transitive reduction"); C1 has 2 links and C2 has 4; the Mobius tables c1_mu and c2_mu of CausalOrder.lean satisfy the Mobius recursion and c2_mu(d0,d3)=1.

name: Maldacena 1997: large N superconformal field theories and supergravity

name: Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten 1998: the correlator dictionary
